summary: I used the last stretch to actually build and run the harness the paused question asked for, and it corrected my own source-only reading. The first version was self-throttling — it waited for each apply's future, so the FSM never fell behind and the probe measured nothing — and once that wait was removed the slow-FSM trial did show the leak, but at a magnitude far smaller than my earlier part-answer implied: the main-loop probe was answered within a few milliseconds while an apply backlog sat behind it, because the blocking send resumes as soon as the FSM accepts one batch. So the main loop is starved per batch, bounded by the FSM's Apply latency, rather than stalled for the whole backlog; the backlog shows up as commit lag, not as one long stall. That narrowing rests on native feedback, so I recorded it as the question's revised hypothesis and discriminator instead of as a finding, reopened the question as active, and submitted the harness as a retained experiment with its scope stating exactly what it drives: two single-voter clusters, a 25ms Apply delay in one and none in the other, 400 applies fired without waiting for their futures, and VerifyLeader — answered inside the main loop for a single voter — timed against an idle baseline. Both comparisons are declared so the receipt decides the boundary either way, and the correction that the flood must not wait per apply is written into the basis. The earlier source-level bound still stands and is what the measurement qualifies: the send itself has no rejection path, so nothing the library provides defers the work; what the run shows is that the resulting delay per batch is the FSM's own Apply latency. That is where the run ends: three execution-grounded findings with their receipts and scoped limits, four refuted suspicions and one excluded cause with the evidence that settled them, one behaviour entry corrected under its own id, every registered question answered, and this last question left open with a harness and a declared comparison rather than an unmeasured claim.
